title: Top Home Printers That Won't Eat Your Ink (2026)
summary: A concise guide to the best home printers that keep ink costs low in 2026.
method: Selected from CNET, TechGearLab, and PCMag reviews, prioritizing models highlighted for affordability and ink efficiency. Added from Amazon listing details (not from the review sources above): Epson EcoTank ET-1913.
assumptions: Prices are only included when explicitly stated in the source excerpts; otherwise, price is null.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 9125e
why: The HP OfficeJet Pro 9125e delivers super fast printing and scanning with a large paper tray, making it ideal for small offices and home use.
Its quiet operation and reliable Wi‑Fi connectivity ensure a smooth experience without signal loss.
products.best_for: Small offices or home users who need fast, reliable printing and scanning.

products.name: Brother All‑in‑one J1010DW
why: The Brother All‑in‑one J1010DW offers impressive text quality and quiet printing at a budget price.
Its small ink cartridges and Amazon Dash button readiness make it convenient for frequent users.
cons: Small ink cartridges may need frequent refills
products.best_for: Budget‑conscious home users who need basic printing, scanning, and copying.
products.skip_if: You require high‑volume printing or photo quality.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-1913 Supertank Printer
why: It comes with enough ink to print up to 3,600 black and 6,500 color pages.
It prints at 11 pages per minute black, has a 100-sheet paper tray and refillable ink tanks.
specs: Up to 3 years of ink in the box
products.skip_if: You need fast printing or a document feeder
products.benefit: Picture a home with a printer that sat unused and dried out its cartridges: the EcoTank uses refillable tanks and keyed bottles so refills are simple. The ink in the box covers up to 3 years of printing. Epson calls it its most affordable supertank. The catch: it is a new model with very few ratings, and 11 pages per minute is not fast.
